rows.note: Use 拗 as the all-purpose colloquial verb for disagreeing or arguing with someone.

example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 tung4 ngo5 ngaau3 laa1

rows.note: Use 嗌交 specifically for having a quarrel or an angry argument.

example.english: They argue over trivial things all the time.
example.traditional: 佢哋成日為咗啲小事嗌交。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 seng4 jat6 wai6 zo2 di1 siu2 si6 aai3 gaau1

rows.note: Use 顯示 when evidence indicates or points to a conclusion rather than when people debate.

example.english: This result indicates that we can argue our method is right.
example.traditional: 呢個結果顯示我哋可以話我哋嘅方法係啱嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 git3 gwo2 hin2 si6 ngo5 dei6 ho2 ji5 waa6 ngo5 dei6 ge3 fong1 faat3 hai6 ngaam1 ge3

rows.note: Use 提出 when presenting a viewpoint, point, or argument for consideration.

example.english: They put forward a new point to argue for at the meeting.
example.traditional: 佢喺會議上提出咗一個新觀點。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 tai4 ceot1 zo2 jat1 go3 san1 gun1 dim2
